rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L01.html Definition 6.3 (lines 268-277) and the e-value paragraph (line 279)
rows.evidence: unchanged since 45fff85 (git diff checked); round-17 evidence: The definitions are complete: an e-value is E >= 0 with E_0[E] <= 1 under every null distribution; a test supermartingale has M_0 = 1, M_t >= 0, each M_t a function of Y_1..Y_t, and E_0[M_t | Y_1..Y_{t−1}] <= M_{t−1}, with equality for a test martingale. The deduction E_0[M_t] <= E_0[M_{t−1}] <= ... <= 1 uses only the tower property of elementary conditional expectation (M4), with nonnegative variables throughout, and Markov gives P_0(E >= 1/α) <= α·E_0[E] <= α. Correct, and nothing beyond M4 is used.

unchanged since 45fff85 (git diff checked); round-17 evidence: Re-derived step by step. B_k = {M_j < h for all j <= k}, B_{−1} = Ω, A_k = B_{k−1} \ B_k; the A_k are disjoint, their union is {max_{k<=n} M_k >= h}, and A_k, B_k are functions of Y_1..Y_k. For W_n = Σ_{k<=n} M_k·1_{A_k} + M_n·1_{B_n}, A_n ∪ B_n = B_{n−1} (disjoint) gives W_n − W_{n−1} = (M_n − M_{n−1})·1_{B_{n−1}}. Taking out what is known gives E_0[W_n − W_{n−1}] = E_0[1_{B_{n−1}}(E_0[M_n|past] − M_{n−1})] <= 0, with integrability from E_0[M_t] <= 1, and W_0 = M_0 = 1. W_n >= h·1{max >= h}, so P(max_{k<=n} M_k >= h) <= 1/h; then continuity from below; then the h' < h argument extends the bound to {sup >= h}. Complete, and it needs no optional-stopping theorem (M6). The supermartingale version generalizes the cited test-martingale Eq. (8) and is proved on the page.

unchanged since 45fff85 (git diff checked); round-17 evidence: Re-derived from scratch (line 440 changed). With A_n the event that some look among the first n rejects (Proposition 6.1), A_n is contained in A_{n+1}, so an added look can only add rejections, with extra probability P(A_{n+1} minus A_n). For normal data that difference contains the open set {|S_t| < b_t for t <= n, |S_{n+1}| > b_{n+1}} for any finite positive boundaries b_t: it is nonempty (y_1 = ... = y_n = 0, y_{n+1} = 2 b_{n+1}) and the density of (Y_1, ..., Y_{n+1}) is positive everywhere, so the probability is positive. A design whose rejection probability already equals alpha (all of alpha spent) therefore exceeds alpha when the look is added. The paragraph states the qualifiers 'for normal data' and 'a design that has spent all of alpha'. Sanity check by simulation (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-quant-phd/cdd15252-4236-59f9-8fa8-e63e41e1dc0d/scratchpad/verify9-L01-L02/extralook.py, 2,000,000 normal null paths, seed 9): a constant two-sided boundary c = 2.4119 on |Z_t| over 5 looks calibrated to total size 0.05000; adding a sixth look at the same boundary raises the rejection probability to 0.05532 (+0.0053), i.e. above alpha, as the argument says. The two numbers in the paragraph are in L01-num-rem69.

unchanged since 45fff85 (git diff checked); round-17 evidence: (a) Independence under every null distribution gives E_0[∏E_i] = ∏E_0[E_i] <= 1. (b) M_{t−1} is known and nonnegative given the past, so E_0[M_t|past] = M_{t−1}·E_0[B_t|past] <= M_{t−1}; L_t(λ) is the case B_t = e^(λY_t − λ²/2), whose conditional mean is exactly 1 by the normal MGF. (c) U ~ U(0,1), E_1 = E_2 = 2·1{U <= 1/2}: means 1, product mean 2. (d) A mixture restarted each quarter on that quarter's returns, with iid days, is an e-value given earlier quarters, so the running product is a test supermartingale in quarterly time and Theorem 6.4 applies (Definition 6.3 and the Ville proof do not need scalar Y). All correct.

rows.evidence: unchanged since 45fff85 (git diff checked); round-17 evidence: Re-checked from scratch. The false equality sentence (continuous-path test martingales with unbounded total variation) is gone: grep of L01.html, L02.html and cards.json for 'Brownian', 'total variation', 'continuous-time', 'continuous-path', 'with equality' finds nothing relating to Ville's inequality, so no out-of-closure SC1 concept enters. The T span now reads 'In discrete time a further gap comes from overshoot: at its first crossing a test martingale is typically strictly above 1/alpha' and matches Ramdas et al. arXiv v2 section 2.5: 'continuous path martingales equal 1/alpha at the instant of crossing it (they do not overshoot), but discrete time (and thus discrete path) test martingales are typically strictly larger than 1/alpha at the first time of crossing; this causes some looseness' (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-quant-phd/cdd15252-4236-59f9-8fa8-e63e41e1dc0d/scratchpad/verify8-L01-L02/dl/ramdas_raw.txt lines 467-500). The page then adds its own derivation for the monitor (4); that derivation is checked in L01-math-lab4-overshoot-inequality. For the monitor, M_k = 1/alpha iff |S_k| = b_k by Proposition 6.6(3), and S_k ~ N(0, k) under H0 has a density, so P(|S_k| = b_k) = 0 and, since M_0 = 1 < 1/alpha, the first crossing exceeds 1/alpha almost surely. The sentence now overreaches nowhere.

rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L02.html Problem P4 solution, 'A false rejection' (lines 443-445)
rows.evidence: unchanged since 45fff85 (git diff checked); round-17 evidence: Re-derived. Almost surely every q_j > 0 (q_j = 0 only for one value of U), so the i - 1 zeros are p_(1) = ... = p_(i-1) = 0 and p_(i) = min_j q_j belongs to a true null. Zeros pass steps 1, ..., i - 1 because the constants are positive (the step fails only when p_(k) > c_k). If min_j q_j <= c <= c_i, step i passes, so the first failing index is > i and H_(i), a true null, is rejected. Hence FWER >= P(min q <= c) = m'c = min(m' c_i, 1) > alpha (m' c_i > alpha by hypothesis, 1 > alpha). The page states it as an inequality; the equality FWER = min(m' c_i, 1) also holds (step i is then decisive: it passes iff min q <= c_i, and the arcs of length c_i cover the circle when c_i >= 1/m'), which I confirmed numerically; the lesson does not need it. [git diff 202ea24..50d202e changes course/modules/S/S7/L02.html at line 88 only (the fwer-growth caption); the passage of this row is outside that line.]

rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L02.html Problem P4 solution, 'Zeros are a convenience' (line 448)
rows.evidence: unchanged since 45fff85 (git diff checked); round-17 evidence: Re-derived. False-null p-values in (0, delta] with delta <= c_j for all j < i: on {delta < min_j q_j <= c} the i - 1 smallest p-values are the false nulls' (each <= delta <= its constant, so steps 1..i-1 pass) and p_(i) = min q <= c <= c_i passes, so a true null is rejected. For delta <= c, P(delta < min q <= c) = m'(c - delta) because the arcs of length delta (<= c <= 1/m') are also disjoint; it exceeds alpha iff delta < c - alpha/m'. rows.evidence: unchanged since 45fff85 (git diff checked); round-17 evidence: Checked sentence by sentence. (1) 'A step-down procedure with fixed constants that controls the FWER at level alpha under every joint distribution of valid p-values must have c_k <= alpha/(m + 1 - k) for every k': the contrapositive of the main result (positive constants, alpha < 1). (2) 'Raising constants only adds rejections, because the first failure moves later, so Holm's procedure rejects everything such a procedure rejects, for every vector of p-values': if c_k <= Holm_k for all k then p_(k) > Holm_k implies p_(k) > c_k, so the first failing index of the c-procedure is no later than Holm's and it rejects a subset. (3) 'A gain beyond Holm's needs the dependence between the tests (Lessons 4 and 5)': true for the class the problem treats (p-value step-down with fixed constants, every configuration of true nulls possible, only marginal validity). Outside that class gains can come from logical relations between the hypotheses (Shaffer 1986) as well as from dependence; the sentence is a pointer, sits after the sentence that fixes the class, and is not a graded claim span. unchanged since 45fff85 (git diff checked); round-17 evidence: New sentence: 'testing each hypothesis at α/m holds the family-wise error rate at or below α for every m, and here, with independent nulls, at exactly α only when m = 1.' Derivation: by Boole's inequality (as in the proof of Theorem 2.2), the FWER of m true nulls each tested at α/m is at most m·(α/m) = α for any dependence, so 'at or below α for every m' holds. With independent true nulls, FWER = 1 − (1 − α/m)^m. Bernoulli's inequality (1 − x)^m ≥ 1 − mx holds with strict inequality for m ≥ 2 and 0 < x < 1, so FWER < α for m ≥ 2; at m = 1 the FWER is exactly α. Numerical check (scratch scripts/card_numbers.py, python -I, .venv): for α = 0.01..0.10 and m = 1..200, 500, 1000, 5000: 0 violations of FWER ≤ α; strictly below α for every m ≥ 2; |FWER − α| ≤ 1e-15 at m = 1. rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L02.html Remark 3.5 claim span (line 272, data-cite romano2005stepwise) and key-results row 8 (line 530); the counter-evidence search for the grade B
rows.evidence: unchanged since 45fff85 (git diff checked); round-17 evidence: Method (round 12, 2026-10-19 to 2026-10-20). Question: does any published work contest the claim that the Romano-Wolf stepwise bootstrap controls the FWER asymptotically with more power than single-step methods (L02 Remark 3.5 and key-results row 8)? Sources, each fetched this round with a User-Agent header only (no e-mail, no mailto, no key). (1) OpenCitations index v2, https://api.opencitations.net/index/v2/citations/doi:10.1111/j.1468-0262.2005.00615.x: 711 citing rows; 708 distinct citing DOIs; 3 rows are arXiv IDs only (1812.04345, 2103.09603, 2107.10017). (2) Crossref work records for the 708 DOIs: 707 resolved; 1 DataCite dataset DOI (10.4225/03/5935ff87c8d5c) returned 404; 298 carry an abstract. The RW record has is-referenced-by-count 770, so about 60 Crossref-counted citers are outside OpenCitations; Crossref has no citers filter (reference.doi and reference-doi are rejected with HTTP 400), so those were not screened. (3) OpenAlex cites filter for W3123939061: HTTP 429 until the daily reset at 00:00 UTC, then HTTP 200 with count 1013 (pages 1 to 6 by offset; cursor paging needs a key, which was not requested): 972 with a DOI (968 distinct), of which 658 are in the OpenCitations set and 310 are OpenAlex-only; 607 carry an abstract. (4) Screens: title or abstract matches the key set (multiple testing, power, Romano, Wolf, step-down, stepwise, Holm, Bonferroni, FWER, single-step, StepM, reality check): 159 of 707 Crossref records and 178 of 1013 OpenAlex works. Contest set (Romano, Wolf, step-down, stepwise, Holm, Bonferroni, family-wise, FWER, single-step, StepM, reality check) in title or abstract: 39 Crossref records; 13 further OpenCitations records through OpenAlex abstracts (for 151 of the 409 records without a Crossref abstract); 16 OpenAlex-only works. (5) Contest-set records without a Crossref abstract were checked against OpenAlex (13 of them have one, read in (4)). The rest were screened by title and venue: applications (Empirical Economics 2015; Decision Support Systems 2010); method papers whose titles make no power claim about Romano-Wolf (Journal of Statistical Planning and Inference 2014; Statistics and Probability Letters 2016 twice; SSRN 2016); and the JFEC 2014 record, whose publisher abstract is read in (6) from OpenAlex. 258 of the 409 records without a Crossref abstract have no abstract in either source and were screened by title only. (6) Abstracts and texts read, with verdicts. Hansen (2005, SSRN 264569; JBES 2005): the SPA test is more powerful than White's single-step Reality Check; not about Romano-Wolf; no contest. Hsu, Hsu and Kuan (SSRN 1087044; JEF 2010, doi 10.1016/j.jempfin.2010.01.001): the stepwise SPA test 'is more powerful than the stepwise Reality Check test of Romano and Wolf (2005)'; a stepwise-versus-stepwise comparison; no contest (the JEF page returned a captcha, so the SSRN abstract was read). Hsu, Kuan and Yen (JFEC 2014, doi 10.1093/jjfinec/nbu014; abstract from the OpenAlex journal record): Step-SPA(k) is 'more powerful than Step-RC(k) under any power notion defined in Romano and Wolf (2005)'; no single-step comparison; no contest (the Oxford University Press page is a Cloudflare challenge, HTTP 403). Market-timing rule performance (JFEC 2011, doi 10.1093/jjfinec/nbq032): applies the RC, SPA and stepwise tests; no RW-versus-single-step comparison; no contest. Survey expectations and adjustments for multiple testing (JEBO 2024): 'The Bonferroni correction and related approaches ... are conservative and result in low power when the null hypotheses are false'; supports the page's comparison; not a contest. Frontiers in Applied Mathematics and Statistics (2023, doi 10.3389/fams.2023.1151314; full text read): 'in all scenarios we considered, Romano and Wolf's method uniformly outperformed methods other than the one we propose' (Bonferroni, Holm, minP and Westfall-Young step-down among them); corroborates. Clarke, Romano and Wolf (2020, Stata Journal, doi 10.1177/1536867x20976314; PDF read): the correction is 'considerably more powerful than earlier multiple-testing procedures, such as the Bonferroni and Holm corrections'; corroborates. arXiv 2107.10017 (2021 preprint on cluster-randomised trials; abstract read): 'the Romano-Wolf type procedure ... is more efficient than the other methods in a simulation-based study'; corroborates (preprint). Harvey and Liu, 'False (and Missed) Discoveries in Financial Economics' (arXiv 2006.04269, 2020; abstract read): 'Evaluating current methods, we find that they lack power to detect outperforming managers'; a general claim about current methods with no RW-versus-single-step comparison in the abstract; not a contest as scoped; the Journal of Finance full text was not read. Harvey and Liu's evaluation for finance (RAPS 2020, doi 10.1093/rapstu/raaa003): the abstract states no finding; the full text is behind an OUP challenge (HTTP 403); not read. Extended MinP tests (arXiv 1911.04696; Econometric Reviews 2026): combination tests; no RW power claim. Testing many moment inequalities (WP 2013): Bonferroni and multiplier-bootstrap critical values; no RW comparison in the abstract. The Stepwise Cauchy Combination Test (JFEC 2025, doi 10.1093/jjfinec/nbaf020; Crossref abstract): 'more powerful than conventional multiple testing corrections'; a newer competitor, not a contest of Romano-Wolf against single-step methods (freshness flag). (7) Result: no contest found in any screened source. Limits, stated plainly: about 60 Crossref-counted citers are not in the OpenCitations list and were not screened; 258 records have no abstract; the RAPS 2020 full text and the Econometrica, JFEC 2014 and JEF 2010 publisher pages were not readable (HTTP 403 or captcha). These limits are recorded in the registry flags. rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L02.html Problem P2 solution, line 421, the shifted construction
rows.evidence: unchanged since 45fff85 (git diff checked); round-17 evidence: Re-derived at 535fd80 with s = alpha/2 and p2 = (U + s) mod 1. For U in [0, 1 - s): p2 = U + s > s, so p2 <= s only at U = 0 (p2 = s). For U in [1 - s, 1): p2 = U + s - 1 in [0, s), so p2 <= s. Hence {p2 <= s} = {0} u [1 - s, 1) (exact on the 160000-point rational grid: p2_recheck_535fd80.out section 2, 'A2 equals {0} u [1 - alpha/2, 1) on the grid: True'). Since s < 1 - s for alpha < 1, {U <= s} n {p2 <= s} = {0}, a null set. P(A1) = P(A2) = s, P(A1 n A2) = 0, so P(union) = 2s = alpha. The text 'which meets {U <= alpha/2} only at the null point U = 0, so the two events are disjoint up to a null set and the FWER is again exactly alpha' is TRUE. Monte Carlo: section 3 (mean over 20 seeds of 1,000,000 draws: 0.050002 +- 0.000035). Round-15 FAIL (L02-math-P2-shift-disjoint PASS in round 15) re-checked and still PASS.

rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L02.html Problem P2 solution, line 421 ('E[U((U+s) mod 1)] = 1/3 - s(1-s)/2 ... correlation 1 - 6s(1-s)')
rows.evidence: unchanged since 45fff85 (git diff checked); round-17 evidence: Derivation at 535fd80. V = (U + s) mod 1 equals U + s on [0, 1-s) and U + s - 1 on [1-s, 1]. E[UV] = int_0^{1-s} u(u+s) du + int_{1-s}^1 u(u+s-1) du = [(1-s)^3/3 + s(1-s)^2/2] + [1/3 - (1-s)/2 + (1-s)^3/6] = (1-s)^2/2 + 1/3 - (1-s)/2 = 1/3 - s(1-s)/2 (using (1-s)^3/2 + s(1-s)^2/2 = (1-s)^2/2 and (1-s)^2/2 - (1-s)/2 = -s(1-s)/2). With E U = E V = 1/2 and Var U = Var V = 1/12 (V uniform), Cov = 1/12 - s(1-s)/2 and corr = 12 Cov = 1 - 6s(1-s). Numerical check: p2_recheck_535fd80.out section 1 evaluates both identities with Fraction arithmetic at 28 rational shifts (k/13, k/97, 1/2, 1/40, 1/20, 1/10, 3/7, 1/4, 2/9, 7/11): both hold exactly at every point (printed: 'points tested: 28'). E[UV] and corr are polynomials of degree at most 3 in s, so 28 exact agreements cover the family. PASS.

rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L01.html section 7, bullet 2 (line 448): 'a 50-day versus a 55-day lookback, which share 50 of their 55 days, can be highly correlated'
rows.evidence: unchanged since 45fff85 (git diff checked); round-17 evidence: Checked at 6dc5f93. (a) Shared days: the 50-day window is the last 50 days of the 55-day window, so the windows share 50 of 55 days (set check: range(5, 55) of range(0, 55) has 50 elements; both windows end on the same day). (b) Possibility, not frequency: under i.i.d. returns with variance sigma^2, Cov(S50, S55) = 50 sigma^2 (the shared part), Var(S50) = 50 sigma^2, Var(S55) = 55 sigma^2, so corr = 50 / sqrt(50 x 55) = sqrt(50/55) = 0.953463. Monte Carlo (2,000,000 draws of 55 i.i.d. normals, scripts/line129_lab1_50_55.py, output line129_lab1_50_55.out): 0.95341. So 'can be highly correlated' is supported by a computed case under i.i.d. returns, and the sentence claims only that the case is possible. PASS.

rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L02.html section 5 bullet 4 (line 347): 'Recovering that power requires information about the dependence between the statistics, which the bootstrap procedures of Lessons 4-5 estimate'
rows.evidence: unchanged since 45fff85 (git diff checked); round-17 evidence: Re-checked at 45fff85 (the sentence changed from 'requires the joint distribution of the statistics'). The cross-reference is correct: L04 is 'Bootstrapping the Search: White's Reality Check and Hansen's SPA' (stationary bootstrap) and L05 is 'Stepwise Multiple Testing: The Romano-Wolf StepM' (grep at 45fff85: L04 and L05 both name the bootstrap). The claim is a necessity claim for procedures that must control the FWER without knowledge of the dependence: P4 (exact checks) shows that no step-down constant above Holm's can be valid for every joint distribution of valid p-values, so any gain beyond Holm's (the power in the Lab 1 example) needs information about the dependence; this is the sense in which 'requires' holds, and P4's 'What it shows' paragraph says the same ('A gain beyond Holm's needs the dependence between the tests'). The sentence is weaker than the old 'joint distribution' and is supported. Non-blocking: the sentence does not say 'for procedures valid under every dependence'; the context does.

rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L02.html line 129 (the paragraph after Example 2.4), first sentence: 'The bound in (1) is attained when the true-null p-values are uniform and their rejection events {p_i <= alpha/m} are pairwise disjoint up to a null set (Problem P2)'
rows.evidence: unchanged since 45fff85 (git diff checked); round-17 evidence: Re-checked at 45fff85 (line 129 changed: 'disjoint' became 'disjoint up to a null set'). Proof: P(union A_i) = sum_i P(A_i minus union_{j<i} A_j), and P(A_i minus ...) = P(A_i) iff P(A_i and A_j) = 0 for every j < i; so Boole's inequality is an equality iff the pairwise intersections are null (the 'up to a null set' qualifier is exactly right). With uniform true-null p-values, P(p_i <= alpha/m) = alpha/m, so FWER = m0 alpha/m. Construction (P2, exact check p2_p4_exact.out): p1 = U, p2 = (U + alpha/2) mod 1 gives P(A) = P(B) = alpha/2, P(A and B) = 0 and P(A or B) = alpha exactly (alpha = 1/20). Sufficiency is shown; the sentence's 'attained when' is a sufficient condition, which is what it claims.

rows.evidence: unchanged since 45fff85 (git diff checked); round-17 evidence: Same sentence as L02-claim-line129 (re-checked at 45fff85): Boole equality iff pairwise null intersections; P2 construction exact (p2_p4_exact.out). PASS.

rows.evidence: unchanged since 45fff85 (git diff checked); round-17 evidence: Re-checked at 45fff85. rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L02.html line 129, sentence 'In the extreme where all null p-values are one uniform variable, the union of m0 identical events is one event, and Bonferroni's FWER is alpha/m, not alpha.'
rows.evidence: unchanged since 45fff85 (git diff checked); round-17 evidence: Re-checked at 45fff85. If all null p-values equal one uniform U, the m0 events {U <= alpha/m} are identical; their union has probability alpha/m (uniform), which is the value in Problem P1 (exact: m = 50, alpha = 0.05 gives 0.001). Correct.

rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L02.html line 129, sentence 'Problem P2 shows that events disjoint up to a null set can come from positively correlated p-values.'
rows.evidence: unchanged since 45fff85 (git diff checked); round-17 evidence: Re-checked at 45fff85 (P2 solution line 421). With the shift s = alpha/2 (alpha = 0.05): correlation of U and (U + s) mod 1 is 1 - 6s(1-s) = 683/800 = 0.85375 > 0 (exact, p2_p4_exact.out), and the events {U <= s} and {(U+s) mod 1 <= s} meet only at U = 0 (P(A and B) = 0 exactly). So the sentence is true.

unchanged since 45fff85 (git diff checked); round-17 evidence: Re-checked at 45fff85 (line 446 changed: 'the events, disjoint up to a null set, turn Boole's inequality into an equality'). Derivation: with c_i = alpha/m' we have c = alpha/m'; V >= 1 exactly when min_j q_j <= alpha/m' (if p_(i) > c_i the procedure stops with V = 0); FWER = m' . alpha/m' = alpha. rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L02.html Problem R1 solution, line 488 ('of moderate strength')
rows.evidence: The lab's setting (L02 Lab 3, section lines 303-318, hypothesis at line 305; twin lab-S7-L02-3.py): 100 one-sided z-tests, 50 false nulls centred at 3.5, 4000 replications, Bonferroni cut 3.29, seed 3003. The R1 sentence says the lab shows FWER control 'discards about 40% of real effects of moderate strength' and gives the powers only 'with 50 false nulls'. The share missed depends on the effect size and on m; 'at this strength' is the lab's own qualifier (line 338). A z-shift of 3.5 is not a moderate effect for a single unadjusted 5% test (power 1 - Phi(1.645 - 3.5) = 0.968, computed), so 'moderate strength' is both undefined and wrong for the simulated effect.
